description: CyclOSM is a bicycle-oriented map built on OpenStreetMap data. Its style shows the main types of cycle tracks and lanes on each side of the road in urban areas, bicycle parking, road speeds and surfaces, elevators and ramps, touring routes and points of interest for cyclists, which makes the state of mapped cycling infrastructure visible at a glance. It is an open-source project whose tile servers are supported by OpenStreetMap France; three variants exist: the default cached map, CyclOSM live updated every minute for mappers, and a lite overlay. Coverage is worldwide, wherever OpenStreetMap has data; tiles below zoom 12 are regenerated weekly and higher zooms are rendered live and cached for up to 72 hours. Access: web map, a public tile endpoint and layers in apps such as OsmAnd. Licence and cost: free; the style is BSD 3-Clause with some Apache 2.0 parts, the data are ODbL, and tile use follows a fair-use policy. Caveats: the site warns that CyclOSM is not a complete or accurate map and is work in progress, and quality follows local mapping. It is a quick visual check of cycle network data before network or exposure analysis and relates to the OpenStreetMap record in the catalogue, from which the underlying geometry can be extracted.
